newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mutual says planning to cut problem loans.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mutual says planning to cut problem loans.

text.p: Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co, Japan"s sixth biggest life insurer, said on Thursday that it plans to cut its problem loans to manageable levels by the end of the 1997/98 business year.

A spokesman said that the life insurance company intends to cut its problem loans in fiscal 1996/97, which ends this March, and the next business year to March 31, 1998, but that details of the strategy have yet to be worked out.

A Japanese economic daily, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, reported on Thursday that Mitsui Mutual Life is expected to dispose of about 90 billion yen worth of problem loans in 1996/97 and is planning to write off another 40 billion yen in problem loans in 1997/98.

The disposal plan comes as the Ministry of Finance prepares to introduce from 1998/99 a system of monitoring the financial health of insurers based on solvency margins that is similar to banks" capital adequacy ratios, the Nihon Keizai said.
Mitsui Mutual Life has said that it had problem loans worth 180.7 billion yen at the end of September 1996.
